## Overview

A poll can receive both a disconnect and the terminal confirmation for a completed transfer. Dropping every message once the connection is dead loses that confirmation and reports the completed load as a failure.

Extracts **B** from #61667 as [requested in review](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/61667#pullrequestreview-5651552184). Refs #61532.

## Claims

- Validated TransferDone and AbortAck messages already buffered during disconnect settle their matching load.
- Work-starting traffic is still dropped after disconnect, and malformed terminals cannot settle a load.

## Validation

Rebased and tested on main `9cd2e98b595e`, including merged #64300. Used cu130 wheel artifacts from `b2a9480dc7aa` (identical C++/CUDA sources to this base), Python 3.12, PyTorch 2.14.0+cu130, RTX 4060 Ti and NIXL 1.4.1 over UCX TCP localhost.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| P2P and tiering component suites | 467 passed |
| Previously recorded real-weight baseline regression, with only the new tests overlaid | 1 failed for the assertion below |
| Same LLM regression with this fix | 1 passed |
| Full real-weight P2P lifecycle module, including merged C | 2 passed |
| Repository pre-commit hooks, including mypy and CI tethering | Passed |

The real LLM test runs a producer and consumer in separate processes. The producer prefills a 192-token prompt and NIXL transfers its KV. External ZMQ socket fault injection reports a monitor disconnect after the successful TransferDone is received but before session dispatch. The producer sends its ordinary successful completion. The consumer must produce the same four greedy tokens as the producer with zero failed promotions.

Reproduction commands from a configured checkout/venv:

```bash
PYTHONHASHSEED=0 UCX_TLS=tcp,self .venv/bin/python -m pytest -q \
  --confcutdir=tests/v1/kv_offload \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_tiering_offloading.py \
  -k 'not test_inference'

PYTHONHASHSEED=0 UCX_TLS=tcp,self VLLM_USE_FLASHINFER_SAMPLER=0 \
  .venv/bin/python -m pytest -v -s \
  tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/test_p2p_lifecycle_e2e.py::test_inference_uses_completion_buffered_after_disconnect
```

Base failure excerpt:
```text
E AssertionError: [1]
E assert 1 == 0
E + where 1 = sum([1])
```
With the fix: `1 passed`.

Model: real `HuggingFaceTB/SmolLM2-135M` weights at `93efa2f097d58c2a74874c7e644dbc9b0cee75a2`, FP16, eager, greedy sampling, and `VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1`. Model validation covers deterministic generation and fault handling; no task-accuracy or performance claim is made. The existing `v1-kv-offload` Buildkite step selects these tests and its dependency list covers the changed P2P sources. All applicable Python and documentation hooks ran, including mypy, CI test tethering, and commit sign-off checks.

## Details

The dead-connection dispatch guard accepts buffered terminals only after peer Disconnect or socket-monitor death. Local protocol errors, repeated dispatch errors, handshake/lookup deadlines, send errors and abort-ack timeouts disable this exception. Terminal messages still pass their existing validation and match by request ID and round. Work-starting messages retain the previous guard. A malformed terminal also disables subsequent terminals in the same batch, even when a peer disconnect was observed first. AbortAck settles the deferred release established by #64256 without producing a second failed outcome. The data-plane teardown and slot-release contract are unchanged.

Duplicate-work check: this is the explicitly requested split from the original PR. Merged #64256 implements the core timed-out-load/deferred-release work using #63779's API; this PR adds the separate B fix on top of that implementation. The other split fixes can land independently. Relevant open-PR searches were refreshed before submission.

Rendered behavior documentation is updated in `docs/features/kv_offloading_usage.md`. Fresh documentation checks passed through local, GitHub, and web retrieval.

AI assistance: OpenAI Codex assisted implementation, tests, and PR preparation.

### Rebase validation (2026-10-29)

Adapted to #64256's immediate-failure/deferred-release lifecycle. All three split PRs remain independent. The same real-weight regression was rerun on the latest base with only the new tests overlaid, and on this fix; results are shown above. The original #61667 branch remains unchanged.


### Review follow-up (2026-10-30)

Moved the real-weight test into a dedicated P2P lifecycle e2e module, retained CI selection, changed the injected race to the realistic socket-monitor path, and moved the child-exit assertion out of cleanup so it cannot mask the original failure. Added protocol-fault rejection coverage, including a malformed terminal after peer disconnect.

### CI follow-up (2026-11-02)

[Official CI #99189](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99189) exposed overlapping memory profiling when the two real engines initialize on one GPU: the consumer counted the producer's newly allocated cache against its own budget and sized zero blocks. Both engines now use an explicit 64 MiB KV cache budget, retaining concurrent startup, the original timeouts, the real NIXL transfer, exact token comparison and zero-failed-promotions assertion. The same test still fails on main and passes with this PR; 445 P2P/tiering component tests and applicable repository hooks pass. Local verification uses the RTX 4060 Ti environment above; the H200 MIG verdict awaits the next upstream CI run.


### Rebase compatibility (2026-11-03)

Preserved #64300's implementation and real-weight tests while combining the lifecycle module and retaining the explicit 64 MiB cache budget. Before this rebase, the memory-budget fix passed official [Buildkite #99306](https://buildkite.com/vllm/ci/builds/99306). After rebasing: 467 component tests, both lifecycle inference tests and repository hooks passed locally. New-head upstream GPU CI is still pending.

Thanks for splitting this out. The fix itself looks right to me: `ZmqTransport.poll()` can buffer the peer's final `TransferDone` in `_recv_router()` and then `mark_dead()` the connection in `_check_monitors()` during the same sweep, and the old guard dropped that message, so the reap reported a finished load as failed. `on_transfer_done` / `on_abort_ack` only touch client state and never send, results are collected before `_reap_dead_sessions()`, and work-starting messages are still dropped. All good.

Two things before this goes in:

1. **Move the real-model test out of `test_sessions.py`** (inline comment below).
2. **One trust edge case on the relaxed guard** (inline comment below): please confirm the intended behaviour.

Could this move out of `test_sessions.py`, or be dropped? It is the only real-model test in `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/`, and it lands in a unit-test module of ~3,800 lines. It spawns a second engine process, downloads SmolLM2 from HF, has 180 s timeouts, and patches `zmq.Socket.send` / `recv_multipart` for the whole class. It would then run on every `v1-kv-offload` job (H200 MIG 35 GB, two engines at 0.30 memory each).

The parametrized `test_buffered_terminal_settles_load_after_disconnect` already covers both death paths (peer `Disconnect` and monitor `mark_dead`) for both terminals. Also, this e2e test injects `Disconnect` *before* `TransferDone` on the wire, an order a real producer never sends. The realistic race is the monitor path, which only the unit test covers.

If you want to keep an e2e check, a dedicated e2e module, or the P2P e2e matrix (#61846 / fault slice #64511), would be a better home.

Small issue if it stays: `assert producer.exitcode == 0` in the `finally` hides the original failure whenever the `try` body raises.

nodes.body:
Is the trust edge case here intended? The guard now accepts terminals whatever the cause of death, including deaths we declared ourselves. Example: a peer sends a malformed message, `_protocol_error` marks the session dead, and a `TransferDone(success=True)` later in the same batch is now accepted as a successful load from a peer we just judged to be misbehaving. The same applies after our own lookup-timeout or abort-ack-timeout disconnects.

For the race this PR targets (peer `Disconnect` / socket monitor), accepting the buffered completion makes sense. If trusting a peer we already faulted isn't intended, one option is to exempt terminals only when the death came from the peer side (`DisconnectMsg` or the monitor), not from our own protocol-error or timeout verdicts. If it is intended, a short comment explaining why would help.

LGTM, thanks for the quick turnaround. Both review points are addressed, and the `test_sessions.py` unit tests pass locally at 7a104afcb5 (152 passed).

One non-blocking suggestion: `_accept_buffered_terminals` depends on `reason != "peer disconnected"`, which has to match the reason string passed at the `DisconnectMsg` branch exactly. If someone later rewords that reason, the fix silently turns off. A module-level constant for the reason, or a `peer_side: bool` argument to `_mark_dead`, would make that coupling explicit. Fine as a follow-up.

@@ -412,6 +412,10 @@ Runtime handshake for a P2P (or P/D) pull, once the orchestrator has set the key
 6. The producer performs the **NIXL WRITE** transfer and sends **`TransferDone`** with a success status.
 7. On `get_finished`, hits are loaded into GPU as ordinary cache hits; misses are recomputed by the engine.
 
+A transfer completion or abort acknowledgement already received when the
+connection closes still settles its load. Disconnect suppresses messages that
+would start new work; it does not discard these buffered terminal confirmations.
+
 In classic **P/D mode** (`remote_prefiller` set, no `remote_kv_source`), the lookup phase (steps 2–4) is skipped: the decode consumer assumes the prefiller holds all of the request's blocks, so every block `lookup()` returns an immediate hit and the consumer jumps straight to the **`FetchMsg`** in step 5. The `LookupMsg`/`LookupRespMsg` round-trip only happens in P2P mode, where the consumer does not know in advance which blocks the peer has cached.

+def test_inference_uses_completion_buffered_after_disconnect(vllm_runner, monkeypatch):
+    """A completed NIXL transfer must not become a failed promotion on disconnect."""
+    import multiprocessing
+    import socket
+    import threading
+
+    import msgspec.msgpack
+    import zmq
+    import zmq.utils.monitor
+
+    from vllm import SamplingParams, TokensPrompt
+    from vllm.v1.metrics.reader import Counter
+
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_ENABLE_V1_MULTIPROCESSING", "0")
+    monkeypatch.setenv("VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT", "1")
+    ports = []
+    for _ in range(2):
+        with socket.socket() as sock:
+            sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+            ports.append(sock.getsockname()[1])
+    source_id = f"127.0.0.1:{ports[0]}".encode()
+    target_endpoint = f"tcp://127.0.0.1:{ports[1]}".encode()
+    buffered = threading.Event()
+    recv = zmq.Socket.recv_multipart
+    recv_monitor = zmq.utils.monitor.recv_monitor_message
+    injected = False
+
+    def receive_both_before_dispatch(sock, *args, **kwargs):
+        frames = recv(sock, *args, **kwargs)
+        if (
+            sock.getsockopt(zmq.TYPE) == zmq.ROUTER
+            and sock.getsockopt(zmq.LAST_ENDPOINT) == target_endpoint
+            and frames[0] == source_id
+            and msgspec.msgpack.decode(frames[-1]).get("type") == "transfer_done"
+        ):
+            buffered.set()
+        return frames
+
+    def disconnect_after_buffering(sock, *args, **kwargs):
+        nonlocal injected
+        if buffered.is_set() and not injected:
+            injected = True
+            return {"event": zmq.EVENT_DISCONNECTED}
+        return recv_monitor(sock, *args, **kwargs)
+
+    monkeypatch.setattr(zmq.Socket, "recv_multipart", receive_both_before_dispatch)
+    monkeypatch.setattr(
+        zmq.utils.monitor, "recv_monitor_message", disconnect_after_buffering
+    )
+    ctx = multiprocessing.get_context("spawn")
+    ready = ctx.Queue()
+    stop = ctx.Event()
+    producer = ctx.Process(
+        target=_serve_p2p_inference_source, args=(ports[0], ready, stop)
+    )
+    producer.start()
+    try:
+        kwargs = _p2p_inference_kwargs(ports[1])
+        model = kwargs.pop("model")
+        with vllm_runner(model, **kwargs) as runner:
+            reference = ready.get(timeout=180)
+            prompt = TokensPrompt(prompt_token_ids=[3 + i % 100 for i in range(192)])
+            params = SamplingParams(

+                max_tokens=4,
+                ignore_eos=True,
+                extra_args={

+                        "remote_prefiller": {
+                            "remote_host": "127.0.0.1",
+                            "remote_port": ports[0],
+                            "kv_request_id": "buffered",
+                        }
+                    }
+                },
+            )
+            result = runner.llm.generate([prompt], params, use_tqdm=False)[0]
+            assert buffered.is_set()
+            assert result.outputs[0].token_ids == reference
+            failures = [

+                for metric in runner.llm.get_metrics()
+                if isinstance(metric, Counter)
+                and "promotion_job_failures" in metric.name
+            ]
+            assert sum(failures) == 0, failures
+    finally:

+        producer.join(timeout=30)
+        if producer.is_alive():
+            producer.terminate()
+            producer.join(timeout=10)
+        ready.close()
+    assert producer.exitcode == 0

Could this move out of `test_sessions.py`, or be dropped? It is the only real-model test in `tests/v1/kv_offload/tiering/p2p/`, and it lands in a unit-test module of ~3,800 lines. It spawns a second engine process, downloads SmolLM2 from HF, has 180 s timeouts, and patches `zmq.Socket.send` / `recv_multipart` for the whole class. It would then run on every `v1-kv-offload` job (H200 MIG 35 GB, two engines at 0.30 memory each).

The parametrized `test_buffered_terminal_settles_load_after_disconnect` already covers both death paths (peer `Disconnect` and monitor `mark_dead`) for both terminals. Also, this e2e test injects `Disconnect` *before* `TransferDone` on the wire, an order a real producer never sends. The realistic race is the monitor path, which only the unit test covers.

If you want to keep an e2e check, a dedicated e2e module, or the P2P e2e matrix (#61846 / fault slice #64511), would be a better home.

Small issue if it stays: `assert producer.exitcode == 0` in the `finally` hides the original failure whenever the `try` body raises.

inline_comments.body:
Is the trust edge case here intended? The guard now accepts terminals whatever the cause of death, including deaths we declared ourselves. Example: a peer sends a malformed message, `_protocol_error` marks the session dead, and a `TransferDone(success=True)` later in the same batch is now accepted as a successful load from a peer we just judged to be misbehaving. The same applies after our own lookup-timeout or abort-ack-timeout disconnects.

For the race this PR targets (peer `Disconnect` / socket monitor), accepting the buffered completion makes sense. If trusting a peer we already faulted isn't intended, one option is to exempt terminals only when the death came from the peer side (`DisconnectMsg` or the monitor), not from our own protocol-error or timeout verdicts. If it is intended, a short comment explaining why would help.

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks for splitting this out. The fix itself looks right to me: `ZmqTransport.poll()` can buffer the peer's final `TransferDone` in `_recv_router()` and then `mark_dead()` the connection in `_check_monitors()` during the same sweep, and the old guard dropped that message, so the reap reported a finished load as failed. `on_transfer_done` / `on_abort_ack` only touch client state and never send, results are collected before `_reap_dead_sessions()`, and work-starting messages are still dropped. All good.

Two things before this goes in:

1. **Move the real-model test out of `test_sessions.py`** (inline comment below).
2. **One trust edge case on the relaxed guard** (inline comment below): please confirm the intended behaviour.

LGTM, thanks for the quick turnaround. Both review points are addressed, and the `test_sessions.py` unit tests pass locally at 7a104afcb5 (152 passed).

One non-blocking suggestion: `_accept_buffered_terminals` depends on `reason != "peer disconnected"`, which has to match the reason string passed at the `DisconnectMsg` branch exactly. If someone later rewords that reason, the fix silently turns off. A module-level constant for the reason, or a `peer_side: bool` argument to `_mark_dead`, would make that coupling explicit. Fine as a follow-up.
